title.en: Technical Writing for Data and AI Work
title.ar: الكتابة التقنية لأعمال البيانات والذكاء الاصطناعي

tagline: REPLACE: one line under the title: what participants can do after the course
description: Participants write the documents that data and AI work runs on: a README, a design document, a decision memo, an experiment report and a model or system card. Each starts from a repository, a model comparison or an evaluation log and ends with a peer test; one draft is unassisted, another is revised with an assistant, and every claim is checked.
audience: Beginners. Graduates, career changers and computing professionals preparing for Developer or Specialist courses, who can run a Python notebook but have not yet studied AI methods.
prerequisites: Has a small data or code project, own or provided, to document

outcomes.text: Identify the reader, purpose and required sections of five common technical document types, given five scenarios with named readers
outcomes.evidence: an outline per scenario matching the reference structure

outcomes.text: Draft a README that lets a stranger install, run and check a small project, given an undocumented repository
outcomes.evidence: the README and a peer's run log on a clean environment

outcomes.text: Draft a one-page decision memo with options, trade-offs, a recommendation and the conditions that would change it, given a measured comparison of two models on quality, cost and latency
outcomes.evidence: a memo scored on a five-criterion rubric

outcomes.text: Prepare an experiment report and a model card that state uncertainty, results by data slice and known limits, given an evaluation run log
outcomes.evidence: a report and card that pass a peer checklist

outcomes.text: Compare an unassisted draft with an assisted revision for accuracy, clarity and invented content, given the participant's two drafts
outcomes.evidence: a revision log of how each claim was checked

format_note: Workshop: one and a half days of writing labs and a tracked follow-up review
